verses.commentary: In those days and at that time introduces eschatological vision. When God restores Judah and Jerusalem's fortunes. Restoration precedes final judgment. Israel's recovery signals cosmic reckoning.

All nations gathered to the Valley of Jehoshaphat (meaning 'Yahweh judges'). God brings them to trial. The charges: scattering his people, dividing his land. The nations stand accused of crimes against Israel and therefore against God.

Atrocities catalogued. Casting lots for human beings. Trading children for prostitutes and wine. Human life devalued to commodity. Boys and girls bought and sold for immediate pleasure. The callousness shocks.

Tyre, Sidon, Philistia challenged directly. What have you against me? The question implies no legitimate grievance exists. If you seek vengeance, God will return it swiftly on your heads. The retribution will be immediate.
Theft of sacred treasures. Silver, gold, finest possessions taken to pagan temples. Plunder of Jerusalem dedicated to foreign gods. Sacrilege compounded by arrogance.
Jerusalem's people sold to Greeks (Javan). Distance from homeland was the point. Slave traders maximized separation to prevent return. Geography weaponized against covenant community.
God rouses the exiles from where they were sold. Return happens despite distance. What merchants intended for permanent exile, God reverses. Their own actions will rebound on their heads.
Role reversal: oppressors' children sold to Judah, then to Sabeans (Arabia). The slave traders become slaves. The Lord has spoken. Divine word seals the verdict.
Proclamation to nations: Prepare for war! Rouse warriors, mobilize fighters. God summons the nations to their own destruction. They think they attack; they are being gathered for judgment.

Plowshares to swords, pruning hooks to spears. Exact opposite of Isaiah 2:4 and Micah 4:3. For the nations, instruments of peace become weapons. Agriculture serves violence. Let the weak say 'I am strong.' Delusion precedes destruction.
Nations summoned to come quickly and assemble. Prayer inserted: Bring down your warriors, Lord. Human armies gather, but divine warriors descend. The battle is joined between heaven and earth.
Nations roused to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. God takes his seat as judge. All nations on every side face divine tribunal. Universal judgment for universal crimes.

Harvest imagery. Swing the sickle, the crop is ripe. Trample grapes, the winepress overflows. But this harvest is judgment. Wickedness is great. The vintage of divine wrath (Revelation 14:18-20 echoes this).

Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision. The Hebrew word (harutz) can mean decision or verdict. Not the nations' choice but God's decree. The day of the Lord near in the valley. Crisis reaches climax.
Sun and moon darken, stars withdraw light. Cosmic signs accompany divine judgment. When God acts definitively, creation responds. Lights that witnessed wickedness now hide.

The Lord roars from Zion, thunders from Jerusalem. The lion of Judah speaks. Heaven and earth tremble. But amid cosmic shaking, the Lord is refuge and stronghold for his people. Terror for nations, safety for Israel.
Then you will know. Knowledge through experience. God dwells in Zion, his holy hill. Jerusalem becomes holy. Never again will foreigners pass through. The city purified and protected permanently.

Edenic restoration. Mountains drip new wine, hills flow with milk, ravines run with water. A fountain from the Lord's house waters the Valley of Acacias (Shittim). Eden's rivers return. Paradise regained.
Egypt desolate, Edom a waste. Violence against Judah and innocent blood shed require retribution. The ancient oppressor (Egypt) and perpetual enemy (Edom) judged. Historical wrongs finally addressed.
Judah inhabited forever, Jerusalem through all generations. Permanence promised. No more exile, no more desolation. The covenant people secure in covenant land eternally.

Shall innocent blood go unavenged? No, declares God. Divine justice requires accounting. The final word: The Lord dwells in Zion. God's presence, the book's ultimate theme, secures everything. The one who judges also saves. Judgment serves restoration. Zion endures because Yahweh abides.
